channel.title: Sagiv's Knowledge Base
channel.description: Last 10 notes on Sagiv's Knowledge Base

item.title: Coccyx
item.description: Definition The coccyx is a small Bone, and the final segment of the Spinal Column. It is formed of 3,4 or 5 Vertebrae.

item.title: Abdominal Bones
item.description: Overview The Bony framework of the abdomen is primarily concentrated in the posterior and inferior regions, providing a musculoskeletal axis of support for the Trunk and protecting vital internal Organs.

item.title: 02 Lower Limb
item.description: Overview The lower limb is a multijointed appendage directly anchored to the axial skeleton by the sacro-iliac joint and strong ligaments.

item.title: 04 Abdomen
item.description: Overview The abdomen is a roughly cylindrical chamber extending from the inferior margin of the Thorax to the superior margin of the Pelvis and the Lower Limb.

item.title: Abdominal Joints
item.description: Overview The Joints of the abdominal region primarily serve to provide a stable yet flexible framework for the posterior wall, transmit weight from the upper body to the Lower Limbs, and allow for the expansion and contraction of the Trunk during various physiological processes.

item.title: Lumbar Vertebrae
item.description: Definition The 5 lumbar vertebrae are located between the Thoracic Vertebrae and Sacrum.

item.title: Sacrum
item.description: Definition The sacrum is a triangular Bone at the base of the Spinal Column, that forms by the fusing of the sacral Vertebrae (S1-S5) by adulthood.

item.title: Abdominal Anatomical Areas
item.description: Overview The abdomen is a roughly cylindrical chamber and a major body region that extends from the inferior margin of the Thorax to the superior margin of the Pelvis and 02 Lower Limb.

item.title: Abdominal Muscles
item.description: Overview The Muscles of the abdomen form a firm but Flexible wall that houses and protects the abdominal viscera, maintains intra-abdominal Pressure, and assists in vital functions such as breathing and posture.

item.title: Linea Alba
item.description: Definition The linea alba is a fibrous midline structure of the anterior abdominal wall, situated between the Rectus Abdominis.
